question: Can causal exterior memory and a prospective local marker support controlled Test 7 reception forecasts?

method.action: Unchanged frozen SS OCF 1 M b_tt=-K b; exterior elimination and causal de-embedding from two surface sites.
method.units: c=hbar=m=1; radius and time m^-1; a amplitude in m.
method.domain: Radial R=80, h=.05,.025,.0125; independent R=100 control.
method.boundaries: Regular origin; finite Dirichlet exterior beyond causal return; internal interface retains exterior memory.
method.initial_data: Prior three compact supported incident shapes, incoming centered derivative; predictor receives only surface record.
method.solver: RK4 dt=.0025 and independent .00125; Hermite stage interpolation; observations every .0125 and .025 control.
method.tolerances: Local waveform 1e-5; energy 1e-6; prospective event residual/budget 1e-4; absolute convergence criterion and <=.1 uncertainty; see locked criteria.

hypotheses.prediction: Complete causal exterior memory recovers the local history and both prospective events within declared controls.
Acquisition, sampling or prospective event convergence prevents controlled local timing even with the exact interface.

controls.method: Known initial field is propagated locally only after variant prediction lock.
Independently decimate surface and local samples.
Cut incoming drive at16 while retaining exterior memory.
Keep incoming drive but suppress exterior memory.

criteria.pass_if: Every frozen input and variant forecast hash verifies; predictions locked before its source local audit.
criteria.fail_if: A resolved violation of the stated accuracy or integrity gate.
criteria.unresolved_if: Missing events or excessive timing/convergence uncertainty as specified.
criteria.uncertainty: Independent mesh, time, domain, output and surface sampling; direct difference budgets.
